content: Stratford mercer and borough man on High Street
He comes to the house when the shop is refused, names two-and-twenty and thirty, and asks two pounds for his own malt-house when the town's brief is a different matter.
He can sit out a brief, a bailiff and a lord's servant, and never mention the two pounds.
He wants a word carried to the Lord Chamberlain, and he will take a supper with no day on it.
